home.metaDescription: Jaeung Kim, a frontend developer in Seoul who builds screens people want to stay on.
paragraphs: I care a lot about how a screen feels. Most of my time goes into the flow of a product, smoothing it out until people can move through it without ever thinking about it.
Simple on the surface, precise underneath. That's the balance I keep chasing, and the problems that show up along the way are the part I enjoy most.
Away from the keyboard I'm usually on a basketball court, or somewhere outdoors getting my energy back.
This site is my workshop. It's where I try out things I've been wanting to learn, test small ideas, and keep notes on ordinary days.

resume.metaDescription: Resume of Jaeung Kim, frontend engineer: experience, projects, skills, and education.
resume.name: Jaeung (Jae) Kim
intro: I'm Jaeung Kim, a frontend engineer with five years of experience. My current work is an automotive R&D platform that models large-scale engineering data as an ontology, visualizes it as a knowledge graph, and brings thousands of spreadsheets and PDFs scattered across departments into a single place where a question in plain language leads directly to a traceable answer.

In a complex domain, the quality of the interface decides whether the product succeeds. Rather than starting from a feature list, I start by observing how users actually respond and refine the UI/UX from there. A good screen makes the next step obvious without anyone having to explain it.

I apply the same standard to my colleagues' experience. I design consistent structures that the next developer can understand and use immediately, and I document the reasoning behind them. On my current project I own the frontend architecture and development, and I work with designers and backend engineers from the planning stage to set the product direction and the shape of the frontend. Translating between design intent and implementation, and closing the gaps between roles, is the work I do best and enjoy most.

I pick up new tools such as AI quickly, but adoption alone is not the goal. I put more weight on designing how people and AI work together and on making that a shared standard for the team. Building an environment the whole team can use well matters more to me than being the one person who uses it well.

e8ight.platformHeading: Frontend platform architecture and company-wide standardization
platformBullets: Unified the monorepo, shared UI package, Storybook design system, lint and i18n templates, and branching strategy into a single company standard, eliminating setup cost for new projects
Migrated from CRA to Vite and Yarn Berry (PnP) and introduced a Jenkins/Docker CI/CD pipeline, reducing CI build time from 10 minutes to 1–2 minutes (about 80%)
Deployed a self-hosted Sentry instance on an internal server to centralize scattered error logs, with real-time alerts for immediate incident detection
Established the frontend team's first commit-stage quality gate, using husky, lint-staged, and commitlint to enforce lint, format, type-check, and commit conventions

Building an AI-native development environment with 15 custom commands and workflows, role-specific subagents and skills, and verification guardrails, making AI-assisted development the default rather than the exception

hyundai.title: Hyundai Motor R&D data integration platform
hyundai.description: An internal platform that integrates Hyundai Motor R&D data into an ontology-based knowledge graph. Led the overall frontend architecture and personally designed and built the knowledge graph visualization SDK, the LLM chat, and the mapping editor.
sdkBullets: Designed and built the knowledge graph visualization SDK shared by the company's GraphRAG products, separating rendering and the d3-force layout engine into a React-independent core that multiple products reuse
Exposed the engine through a single imperative handle that hides implementation types, giving call sites a stable API that survives internal rewrites and allowing the core to be tested in isolation
Rendered directly to Canvas 2D instead of the DOM, redrawing only while the graph is in motion and halting rendering entirely when it is idle to eliminate wasted computation
Improved label performance and sharpness with hybrid rendering: labels are cached as bitmaps for reuse and switched to direct text drawing at high zoom levels
Kept frequently changing state outside React and propagated updates only on actual data changes, preventing unnecessary re-renders in large lists
Expanded the graph incrementally by neighborhood instead of loading every node at once, canceling superseded requests and discarding late responses so only the latest result is applied
hyundai.llmHeading: LLM chat integrated with the knowledge graph
llmBullets: Routed WebSocket events to per-type handlers for text, reasoning steps, and graph evidence, batching bursts of chunks into a single frame to minimize re-renders
Decoupled receiving from display: a token queue drains at a steady typewriter pace, accelerates automatically when it falls behind, and snaps to the text received so far on stop or error
Parsed completed and in-progress regions separately so only completed text is rendered as markdown, preventing unclosed code blocks and partial formulas from breaking the layout

Generated answers with GraphRAG by traversing the graph's nodes and relations; each answer carries a graph query, so 'show evidence' renders the supporting subgraph on the adjacent canvas for source tracing
mappingBullets: Designed a single mapping model that accepts spreadsheets in arbitrary layouts, so an unfamiliar format is structured into ontology entities without a code change
Built in step-by-step validation, preview, and de-duplication to structurally prevent user error in mappings that require 100% accuracy
Implemented the grid from scratch rather than on an off-the-shelf component while matching the feel of Excel, and saved defined layouts as templates to eliminate repeated work

digitalTwin.title: Digital Twin Federation integrated portal
digitalTwin.description: An integrated portal for a government R&D program, designed and built solo as the sole full-stack engineer. Built an operations shell on a single authentication, authorization, and organization model, and delivered everything from a Next.js 15 App Router frontend to a NestJS backend on schedule.
bullets: Applied SSG, ISR, or SSR per route based on its characteristics, and forced authenticated pages to render dynamically to keep private data out of the static cache
Prefetched data in Server Components and dehydrated it into the client-side TanStack Query cache, so the first screen renders without a loading state and client queries take over subsequent updates
Implemented a Next.js BFF that stores tokens only in HttpOnly cookies and relays them to the backend as a Bearer header, so tokens remain inaccessible even under XSS
Separated access and refresh tokens with rotation, reuse detection, coalescing of concurrent refresh requests, and full invalidation on password change to defend against token theft

Registered JWT verification and RBAC globally through APP_GUARD so a new controller cannot ship without authentication; on token expiry the server redirects to login while the client interceptor refreshes in place to keep the flow intact
Gated security settings behind environment variables so a single deployment image serves both public HTTPS and an internal HTTP network

products.title: In-house product suite (NAXiS, PMIS, NDX Cloud, and others)
products.description: Led frontend development for five in-house products.
naxisBullets: Built a no-code ontology editor on React Flow, delegating infrastructure such as the viewport and events to the library while abstracting the domain logic (entity types, relations, serialization) independently, so library upgrades and domain changes stay isolated from each other
Reduced the visual complexity of hundreds of edges converging on a single node by collapsing them into relation group nodes, with custom SVG edges that automatically merge identical relations
Adopted Dagre for layout while keeping control over when it runs and what it receives, with partial re-layout on expand and collapse to keep interaction cost low
Because the domain logic is separated from the library, several in-house products adopted the editor without modification and it became a shared component asset
pmisBullets: Redesigned a tree of thousands of rows with child-flag-based lazy loading and virtual scrolling, reducing initial load time from 12 seconds to 2 seconds (about 80%)
Parallelized serial drawing uploads with mutateAsync and Promise.all, reducing 19 files from 4 minutes to 20 seconds, with optimistic UI and rollback for immediate feedback
ndxCloudBullets: Abstracted a four-level permission hierarchy (organization, project, site, dataset) into a single RBAC matrix, providing consistent access control down to the screen level

Resolved a 4,000-image upload bottleneck on two fronts: parsing only the JPEG APP1 marker for EXIF extraction cut memory from 20 GB to 800 MB, and presigned URLs connecting the browser directly to S3 cut upload time from 20 minutes to 10 minutes with 70% less server load

bullets: Joined a unified clothing marketplace (e-commerce) startup as its first developer, owning planning, development, deployment, and operation of the entire frontend
Designed and built the e-commerce platform architecture for Shopify Marketplaces integration
Designed the integration of Supabase and third-party (Instagram, TikTok) login kits, improving platform security and sign-in accessibility
Planned and implemented the Shopify Payments gateway integration, reducing cart abandonment and improving transaction success rates
Full-stack developer at an EMR (Electronic Medical Records) SaaS startup
Independently designed and built the architecture of a WebGL-based marketing site, delivering a modern web experience
Designed the interaction and animation strategy with Framer Motion and GSAP, improving the user experience
Designed and operated an HR and attendance admin portal that non-technical executives could use without assistance
Designed the backend API architecture, AWS infrastructure, and MongoDB schema, and built the CI/CD pipeline
Designed a React component architecture and built scalable systems at a cryptocurrency exchange startup
Designed and implemented the credit card payment integration and the cryptocurrency purchase flow
Planned and implemented social media URL preview optimization with AWS Lambda@Edge and Facebook Open Graph
Collaborated with designers to improve the UI/UX architecture and the overall user experience

gantt: Open-source Gantt chart library published on npm, with virtualization and lazy loading that improved rendering performance on thousands of tasks by 40%
Designed a WBS-based project management architecture with an optimistic UI pattern for live edits to structure and schedule
An extensible plugin architecture and a small footprint keep it in production use, with continuous improvement driven by community feedback
portfolio: Static site architecture on the Next.js App Router with SSG, managing projects and a technical blog from a single system
Designed the 3D interaction architecture with WebGL and Three.js and optimized its rendering performance
Improved performance and user experience through an image optimization strategy and a responsive design architecture
bcGovernment: Employee management system architecture built for the BC Government IS24 Full Stack Competition
Designed the data model for organizational hierarchy management and an efficient UI/UX architecture
React frontend, Node.js backend, and PostgreSQL database architecture, containerized and deployed with Docker
lostArk: Discord.js party and raid recruitment bot for Lost Ark that improved matching efficiency in the game community
Command-based event handling architecture and an automatic notification system for user convenience
Runs in a live community, with continuous improvement and maintenance driven by user feedback
